summary: George Le Grand Jacob worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Elizabeth College and under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1820–1821, and taught at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1833 to 1835.

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Catholic University of America (1893–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1940), and founded the Linguistic Society of America.

George Morrison Carstairs studied at the University of Edinburgh (B.M. circa 1936–1941; Dr.Med. circa 1958–1959). He served as Professor of Psychological Medicine at Edinburgh (1961–1973) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of York (1973–1978).

George Payn Quackenbos was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his A.B. (circa 1898–1902) and Ph.D. (circa 1902–1915) from Columbia University, and served as an Instructor in Latin at City College of New York in 1910.

George Perrigo Conger worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Cornell, Union Theological Seminary, Berlin, Jena, Heidelberg, the Sorbonne, and Columbia. He served at the University of Minnesota (1920–1952) and held visiting professorships at Ohio Wesleyan and Calcutta.

George Quasha, active in religious studies and Tibetology, founded Station Hill Press. He taught at Stony Brook University (circa 1968–1971), Bard College (circa 1974), The New School, and Naropa University.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, attested in 1978.
George Read Edward Beresford worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Manager of Cawnpore Bank until 1849, when he became manager of Delhi Bank.
Religious studies scholar George Rupp studied at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He held academic posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (circa 1993–2002).

George Rusby Kaye worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Wyggeston Grammar School and St. Mark's College, taught at Bishop Cotton School, held school rector posts, and worked for the Bureau of Education and India Office.
George Saintsbury studied at King's College School and Merton College, Oxford. He served in a post at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1895 to 1915.

Philosopher George Santayana studied at Harvard, Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge, earning his Ph.D. under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.

George Scott Robertson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Westminster Hospital (circa 1873–1877) and served in the Indian Medical Service (1878) and the Foreign and Political Department (1888).

Linguist and Indologist George Sherman Lane studied at Iowa, Iceland, Paris (under Benveniste, Lévi, Vendryes, and Meillet), and Chicago. He held positions at Chicago, Catholic University of America, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Oslo.

George Shirt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cambridge and the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1866, and was a Fellow of the University of Mumbai.

George Smith worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an LL.D. from the University of Edinburgh (by 1868), was a professor at Doveton College in 1854, and served as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta (1856–1875).

George Speirs Alexander Ranking worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. Educated at Aldenham School and St Catharine's College, Cambridge, he was Lecturer in Persian at Balliol College, Oxford, and Professor of Persian at Calcutta.

Indologist and philosopher George Thibaut studied under Weber, Holtzmann, and Müller, earning a Ph.D. from Berlin. He held leadership posts at Queen's College Benares, Muir Central College, and Calcutta University, and founded The Pandit.
George Turnbull Marshall worked in Indology. He served as Secretary at Fort William College from 1838 to 1852 and as Secretary at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1839 to 1840.

George Turnour worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a civil servant from 1818 and became Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.
